newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Average share prices down on Bucharest exchange.
newsitem.headline: Average share prices down on Bucharest exchange.

text.p: Most average share prices on the Bucharest stock exchange drifted lower on Thursday as investors slipped into a wait-and-see attitude, pulling down two independent bourse indices.
"Buyers felt it was the right time to drive down prices, which in some cases were indeed too high," a trader said.
The VAB and the BIG indices dropped by 3.8 and 3.9 percent respectively from the previous session. The BIG first-tier index slipped 4.13 percent to 3,077.12 points.
The average price of 16 stocks edged down, eight inched up and six had no trade. Six companies were suspended pending announcements.
Turnover gained six million lei to 7.9 billion lei, mainly thanks to a higher turnover level on the first tier, which took some 85 percent of overall turnover.
"Investors were reluctant to pay higher prices even for these high caps, which have always been in demand," another trader said.
Operators said they expected similar investor sentiment on Friday, with the market entering a bearish mood.
"Intensified late trading helped some of the stocks -- including top-tier ones -- close higher," a broker said.
Three of the first-tier listings ended stronger despite lower average prices for two of them.
Azomures fertiliser maker firmed 70 lei to close at 3,300 and pharmaceutical companies Antibiotice ATBE.BX and Terapia gained 100 lei and 50 lei respectively to end at 5,500 and 5,900.
Traders said Terapia was higher in both average and closing quotes because of late trading and thin supply.
Oltchim chemical plant was the top tier's loser, shedding one percent on its average price and closing 30 lei weaker at 2,600.
Policolor dye maker once again took centre-stage on the second tier. It had a special trade worth 276 million lei, which pushed turnover up to 980 million lei. It closed 400 lei firmer at 4,950.
